source: Make a first person shooter where you stand in one place and shoot clay pigeons that are being launched from launchers that are positioned all over so you never know where the next target will come from

layout_placement.text: Clay pigeon launchers sited all around the range at varied distances and angles, deliberately unreadable so the next target can come from any direction
A single fixed firing position where the player stands and pivots to track targets

notes: The player never traverses the map: only the firing position and the ring of launchers need placing.
spawner-npc is written to give defenders a readable direction to hold against; the prompt asks for the opposite, so the text inverts the option's intent.
No preset fit. Every shooter preset is a PvP mode or a lane-network wave defence, both of which contradict a stationary shooter.
Clay pigeons themselves are launched projectiles with no fixed footprint, so they are behaviour rather than placed geometry.

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the range read as a modern outdoor clay range, a military training facility, or something stylized?
answers.answer: Make it a modern outdoor clay shooting range.

answers.ask: Does a round end on a score target, a time limit, or a number of missed targets?
answers.answer: Use a short time limit for each round, with the score based on how many clay pigeons the player shoots.
